automobiles.title: Automobiles
automobiles.text:
In Spanish, there are several ways to say **car**, mainly differing by country/region:

**carro**

**auto**

**coche**

All are correct and understood. We'll generally use **carro** in the app, but be aware that folks you interact with may use a different word.

decir.title: Decir
decir.text:
|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **decir**  | to say |
| **(yo) digo** | I say |
| **(tú) dices** | you say |
| **(él/ella) dice** | he/she says | 
| **(nosotros) decimos** | we say |
| **(ellos) dicen** | they say |

directional-a.title: Directional "a"
directional-a.text: In Spanish, the particle "a" is used to show a direction or destination. It can be used for physically traveling to some place or for performing an action targeted at or for someone.

el-y-la.title: El y la
el-y-la.text: **El** and **la** both translate to "the" in English. However, **el** is used with masculine nouns, while **la** is used with feminine nouns.

grande-vs-gran.title: Grande vs. gran
grande-vs-gran.text:
**Grande** appears after a noun and means *big* or *large*. When it comes in front of a noun, it changes to **gran** and means *great*.

**Un hombre grande** - *a big man*

**Un gran hombre** - *a great man*

**Una gran mujer** - *a great woman*

**Grandes mujeres** - *great women*

hacer.title: Hacer
hacer.text:
|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **hacer**  | to do |
| **(yo) hago** | I do |
| **(tú) haces** | you do |
| **(él/ella) hace** | he/she does | 
| **(nosotros) hacemos** | we do |
| **(ellos) hacen** | they do |

*Note: hacer also means "to make"*

ir.title: Ir
ir.text:
|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **ir**  | to go |
| **(yo) voy** | I go |
| **(tú) vas** | you go |
| **(él/ella) va** | he/she goes | 
| **(nosotros) vamos** | we go |
| **(ellos) van** | they go |

nada.title: Nada
nada.text:
**Nada** means *nothing*, but is also translated as *anything* when used with a negative.

For example, **"No leo nada"** could be translated as either *"I read nothing"* or *"I don't read anything."*

nosotras-y-ellas.title: Nosotras y ellas
nosotras-y-ellas.text: **Nosotras** and **ellas** are translated into English the same as **nosotros** and **ellos**, respectively (meaning "us" and "them"). However, remember that they are only used in Spanish when the entire group of people is female. If there's even one male in the group you're referring to, or your not sure of who is in the group, stick with **nosotros** and **ellos**.

querer.title: Querer
querer.text:
|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **querer**  | to want |
| **(yo) quiero** | I want |
| **(tú) quieres** | you want |
| **(él/ella) quiere** | he/she wants | 
| **(nosotros) queremos** | we want |
| **(ellos) quieren** | they want |

question-words.title: Question words
question-words.text:
**Qué** - what

**Quién** - who

**Cuándo** - when

**Dónde** - where

**Cuál** - which

**Por qué** - why

**Cómo** - how

saber.title: Saber
saber.text:
|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **saber**  | to know |
| **(yo) sé** | I know |
| **(tú) sabes** | you know |
| **(él/ella) sabe** | he/she knows | 
| **(nosotros) sabemos** | we know |
| **(ellos) saben** | they know |

sp-un-una.title: Un y una
sp-un-una.text: "Un" and "una" are articles in Spanish, like "a" and "an" in English. They correspond to grammatical gender, so "a student" is "un estudiante" and "a school" is "una escuela."

tener-to-have.title: Tener (to have)
tener-to-have.text:
Tener is an irregular verb, so it doesn't follow the regular rules for "-er" verbs.

|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **tener**  | to have |
| **(yo) tengo** | I have |
| **(tú) tienes** | you have |
| **(él/ella) tiene** | he/she has | 
| **(nosotros) tenemos** | we have |
| **(ellos) tienen** | they have |
| **(ustedes) tienen** | you (all) have |

unos-y-unas.title: Unos y unas
unos-y-unas.text: One of the ways to say "some" in Spanish is by using "unos" (with masculine nouns) and "unas" (with feminine nouns). For example: **unos perros** *(some dogs)* and **unas casas** *(some houses)*.

venir.title: Venir
venir.text:
|  **Spanish**  |  **English**  | 
| --------- | -------- |
| **venir**  | to come |
| **(yo) vengo** | I come |
| **(tú) vienes** | you come |
| **(él/ella) viene** | he/she comes | 
| **(nosotros) venimos** | we come |
| **(ellos) vienen** | they come |
